name: Artificial Neural Net - Perceptron
catalogPath: Sample Models/Computer Science/Artificial Neural Net - Perceptron
miniText: Which Boolean distinctions can a single learned threshold represent? NetLogo Artificial Neural Net Perceptron trains weighted connections from two inputs and a bias to one output, comparing predictions with a selected target function. Rosenblatt [1] provides the original perceptron framework. Rumelhart and colleagues [2] establish a multilayer alternative, and Cybenko [3] analyzes the expressive power of networks with sigmoidal hidden units. These comparisons clarify why changing learning rate cannot make one linear separator represent exclusive OR. The baseline displays weights, classification boundaries, and training error under repeated examples. Inputs, thresholding, finite examples, and update rules are deliberate simplifications. Failure on a nonseparable task is a representational limitation rather than evidence of faulty training alone. The model illustrates supervised learning and its architectural constraints; it does not reproduce biological neural circuitry or demonstrate generalization to unseen datasets.
